text: Ciénega is a municipality located in the Márquez Province, within the Boyacá Department of Colombia. Its urban center lies on the Altiplano Cundiboyacense, 27 kilometers (17 miles) from Tunja, the departmental capital, at an elevation of 2,460 meters (8,070 feet). The elevation within the municipality varies between 2,200 meters (7,200 feet) and 3,400 meters (11,200 feet). It shares borders with Viracachá and Soracá to the north, Rondón to the east and south, and Ramiriquí to the south and west. The name Ciénega originates from the Chibcha language and translates to "Place of water." Prior to the Spanish conquest, the region was part of the Muisca Confederation, a collection of independent rulers, with Ciénega under the rule of the zaque based in Hunza. Conquistador Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada passed through Ciénega on his journey to the mythical El Dorado. Modern Ciénega was officially established on October 22, 1818, by José Cayetano Vasquez, the son of the owner of the main hacienda in the area. The primary economic activities in Ciénega are livestock farming, which accounts for 66%, and agriculture, which makes up 31%. Agricultural products grown in the region include potatoes, maize, peas, arracacha, tree tomato, and uchuva.
